items.body:
### What happened?

I have built some docker images and pushed them to my dockerhub repo. That means that these docker images are also available on my local computer. Here is an example of a public docker image in my repo https://hub.docker.com/repository/docker/vikash112/pathology/general

I wrote a yaml file for a pod that uses this image and I keep getting the following error
![image](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/assets/3863212/92c308c4-d1e6-417c-8511-68d79f8344e7)

Now, the interesting thing is that 
1. Because the image is available locally, k8s should not try to download the image 
2. So, inorder to force k8s to not download the image, I used the `imagePullPolicy: Never` and I get the following error, even though the image is clearly present
![image](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/assets/3863212/7cff6583-9062-4ec5-8ee3-b3e24b15175f)

So, another thing I tried was to create a secret in k8s for my docker login following the instructions here https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/configure-pod-container/pull-image-private-registry/

However, I am able to pull the public repositories like `mongodb`, `busybox` etc. So, I don't know why my own public repositories have any problems while pulling. 

Any help will be very very appreciated. 
Thanks 





### What did you expect to happen?

I dont expect k8s to pull any images if they are available locally. If it is trying to pull it should pull my images from docker hub as it is pulling other images like `mongodb`, `busybox` etc.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

You can try it using the following yaml script
```
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: classification-pod
spec:
  restartPolicy: OnFailure
  containers:
    - name: caiiapp
      image: vikash112/pathology:0.1.0
      imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent
      resources:
        limits:
          nvidia.com/gpu: 1
  nodeSelector:
    kubernetes.io/hostname: digi1036734
```

Lets say you save the file as myscript.yaml. You can execute it as 
```
kubectl apply -f myscript.yaml
```
